_comment: The watermark configuration this lab implements.
Every value here is PUBLISHED, and the keys are not this lab's invention: they are the
DEFAULT_WATERMARKING_CONFIG shipped in google-deepmind/synthid-text @ addb4a1
(src/synthid_text/synthid_mixin.py). They are demonstration keys in a public
repository. A real deployment keeps the whole block secret, because anyone holding it
can score text with it, mark text with it, or strip the mark from text.
Parameter names follow that repository, not this lab's preferences. Its own comment on
ngram_len reads: 'This corresponds to H=4 context window size in the paper.'
A second, genuinely different reference implementation of the same scheme.
transformers 5.15.1 seeds its hash chain with the literal 1 and reads g-values from a
table of random bits built by a torch RNG. The official repository removed that table
in PR #32. Both are implemented here so the lab can show that two faithful
implementations, given the same text and the same keys, do not read each other's marks.
temperature and top_k are applied by the reference logits processor itself: it scales
the scores, takes the top k, watermarks within that candidate set, and samples from
the result. So the distribution the tournament acts on is already a top-k
distribution, and this lab never calls it the model's unmodified distribution.
min_new_tokens equals max_new_tokens, which suppresses the end-of-text token until the
target length so the watermarked and control samples are the same length and differ in
the watermark alone. That is a real constraint on the sampling distribution and is
recorded rather than hidden.
